accordion.use: Let readers scan a set of independent questions and expand those relevant to them.
accordion.avoid: Show mandatory instructions and short, sequential procedures directly on the page.
accordion.access: Use meaningful trigger names, preserve heading order and let readers toggle each section by keyboard.
accordion.content: Use a specific question or topic per heading. A single question should introduce one answer in each language.
keys: Expand or collapse the focused section.
Focus the first or last heading.

ahv-input.use: Collect a Swiss social insurance number in a workflow that requires the personal identifier and its check digit.
ahv-input.avoid: Use UidInput when identifying a Swiss enterprise and a separate reference for a customer account.
ahv-input.access: Provide the expected grouped format in a persistent hint and support pasting all digits. Use synthetic numbers in shared examples.
ahv-input.content: Use the local name of the social insurance number. Give the 756 prefix and grouping once in the hint.
keys: Enter or leave the field. A valid identifier is formatted when focus leaves.
Type, select, paste and correct the value with the platform’s editing keys.

alert.use: Keep an explanation visible when an interruption changes what someone can do on the page.
alert.avoid: For a routine save with no follow-up, a brief status is sufficient. Repeated alerts interrupt reading.
alert.access: Keep the heading in document order. Reserve live alert announcements for information that arrives after the page has loaded.
alert.content: State the event and a feasible next step in one or two short sentences. Avoid blame and internal error codes as the headline.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

alert-dialog.use: Ask for an explicit decision before deleting a record or discarding work that cannot be recovered.
alert-dialog.avoid: Routine saves and reversible display changes can proceed without interrupting the person.
alert-dialog.access: State the consequence in the description. Keep the safe action reachable and return focus sensibly after cancellation or deletion.
alert-dialog.content: Name the object in the question and use an unambiguous verb for confirmation. Keep the consequence to one plain sentence.
keys: Open the confirmation from its trigger. Initial focus goes to Cancel.
Move between actions within the modal.
Cancel and return focus to the trigger.

app-shell.use: Give a workspace a consistent header, navigation area and main reading area across several routes.
app-shell.avoid: Use a single document layout for a printed letter or an isolated embeddable widget.
app-shell.access: Provide one main landmark, a skip target and a descriptive page heading. Keep the same navigation order between routes.
app-shell.content: Use the product name once in the header. Reserve the main heading for the task or record currently open.
keys: Activate the skip link to focus the main content.
Open or close the mobile index from its button.
Close the open mobile index and focus its button.

aspect-ratio.use: Reserve the final shape of a photo, film or diagram as its container changes width.
aspect-ratio.avoid: A fixed aspect ratio clips variable-length copy and forms. Let text determine their height.
aspect-ratio.access: Give the contained image an appropriate alternative and preserve the edges of maps or diagrams used for instructions.
aspect-ratio.content: Describe the useful subject in a brief alternative. Leave the decorative frame unlabelled and put extended context in a caption.

example.good: Entrance on the south side of the station

keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

attachment.use: Link to a real file that someone can open or download, such as a meeting agenda.
attachment.avoid: A form that collects files needs an upload input and feedback about accepted formats.
attachment.access: Use the document name in the link. Add the format and size where they can be read alongside it.
attachment.content: Name the subject and edition first. Put file details after the title and retain official names in translated versions.
keys: Open or download the file according to the link and browser settings.
Paste clipboard files when the upload field has focus.

avatar.use: Identify a sender or account visually when a portrait or initials aid recognition.
avatar.avoid: A photo by itself cannot distinguish homonyms or identify someone in a consequential approval step.
avatar.access: Provide the person's name. Mark the avatar decorative if the adjacent name already identifies the same person.
avatar.content: Use the name the person supplies, including accents. Translate the role or team next to it and allow long names to wrap.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

badge.use: Put a brief state next to the record it describes, such as an invoice awaiting payment.
badge.avoid: Use an Alert when the reader needs an explanation or a next action.
badge.access: Spell out the state. Check that the same text still distinguishes the records in forced colours.
badge.content: Use a short state such as a single adjective. Keep the same grammatical form across the badges in a list.
keys: Follow the destination when composed as a link. A plain badge is read as text.

bar-chart.use: Compare the magnitude or signed change of independent categories against a shared zero baseline.
bar-chart.avoid: Use LineChart for change through time and a table when readers need to look up many exact values.
bar-chart.access: Give the figure a subject and unit. Supply category labels and an equivalent data table that preserves negative values.
bar-chart.content: Name the measure and period in the title. Keep place names intact and put the unit next to the values or in the column heading.
keys: Focus the data-table disclosure when readings are available.
Show or hide the same values in the accessible table.

breadcrumb.use: Show where a page sits within a hierarchy that visitors can follow back up.
breadcrumb.avoid: Use a Back action for history-dependent navigation and Steps for progress through a sequential form.
breadcrumb.access: Give the trail a navigation name. Identify the current location and keep dividers out of link names.
breadcrumb.content: Use the short destination name at each level. Keep parent and child distinct even when their translated names share a prefix.
keys: Move between links in document order.

bubble.use: Separate individual utterances within a conversation whose speakers are already identified.
bubble.avoid: A system-wide notice, policy or detailed instruction deserves a persistent section outside the conversation.
bubble.access: Identify the author in text. Start and end alignment alone cannot communicate who wrote a message.
bubble.content: Keep one thought per message and preserve the original language when quoting someone. Short sentences survive narrow screens.

example.good: Your document is ready for collection.

keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

button.use: Submit, save or change something in the current task. A payment instruction benefits from naming the object of the action.
button.avoid: Use a TextLink for a destination visitors should be able to open in a new tab.
button.access: Give icon-only buttons a name. Keep the action name visible while work is pending and expose the outcome near the form.
button.content: Use a verb and its object. Aim for one short phrase in each language and let the button grow for the longest translation.
keys: Activate an enabled button. When composed as a link, use Enter to navigate.

button-group.use: Present closely related actions on the same object, such as printing or downloading its receipt.
button-group.avoid: Separate a destructive action from a row of routine actions when a mistaken activation would be costly.
button-group.access: Name the group and keep its focus order consistent when buttons wrap to a second row.
button-group.content: Use matching short verbs with objects where needed. Make each action understandable when announced on its own.
keys: Move between enabled controls in the group.

calendar.use: Let people inspect a whole month or compare candidate appointment dates with neighbouring days and holidays.
calendar.avoid: Use a text date field for a known date far from the current month, such as a birth date.
calendar.access: Name the calendar and preserve the focus indicator while moving between dates by keyboard. Give holidays a textual name in addition to the visual mark.
calendar.content: Use the local month name and the full holiday name where space allows. Explain in one sentence what a marked date means for this service.
keys: Move to Monday or Sunday of the current week.
Move to the preceding or following month. Add Shift to move a year.

canton-combobox.use: Find a canton from its name or abbreviation without stepping through all the cantons.
canton-combobox.avoid: Use CantonSelect when a short list is easier to scan than to search.
canton-combobox.access: Provide a visible label, test selecting a suggestion with the keyboard and distinguish an empty search from a confirmed choice.
canton-combobox.content: Keep the query hint to one brief instruction. Use a real abbreviation as an example only if both names and codes work.

copy.fr-CH: Rechercher un nom ou un sigle

keys: Open the list and move the active option.
Close the list. Tab also moves focus out of the field.

canton-select.use: Ask for a Swiss canton from a fixed list in a short form.
canton-select.avoid: Use CantonCombobox for frequent lookups by abbreviation or partial name.
canton-select.access: Associate the select with a visible Canton label. Keep an explicit empty option when a canton has yet to be chosen.
canton-select.content: Use the local name for the field and allow enough width for complete canton names. Keep abbreviations uppercase when displayed.
keys: Focus or leave a closed select.
Move through enabled options in the open picker.
Move to the first or last enabled option in the open picker.
Find an option by its label in the open picker.
Confirm the highlighted option and return focus to the select.
Close the picker and keep the previously selected value.

card.use: Group the identity, details and available actions for one booking or case.
card.avoid: Several unrelated tasks in one card need their own headings or a list with separate links.
card.access: Give the card a meaningful heading. Keep links and buttons as individual focus targets with visible text.
card.content: Lead with the record name. Limit the description to one sentence and allow names in each language to wrap.
keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

carousel.use: Let readers move between related visual examples that make sense one at a time.
carousel.avoid: A list or grid works better when readers need to compare every item before choosing.
carousel.access: Give previous and next controls names and make the current position available in text. Keep navigation usable without a swipe.
carousel.content: Use short directional labels and identify the subject of the slide. Keep the translated caption separate from the position indicator.
keys: Show the previous or next slide while the carousel region has focus.
Show the first or last slide.
Activate a focused slide navigation button.

chart.use: Offer a quick, labelled comparison of values with the underlying data always available.
chart.avoid: For a temporal series, use the line chart. For a dense financial statement, use a table with units and totals.
chart.access: Describe what the categories represent. Keep numeric values in the alternative table even if the graph is hidden or printed.
chart.content: Use a short title that specifies the measure. Keep the category labels parallel and make every axis or column unit explicit.
keys: Focus the data-table disclosure when readings are available.
Show or hide the same values in the accessible table.

chart-table.use: Let readers compare the size of a value and retrieve its exact number in the same row.
chart-table.avoid: Use a simple table for identifiers and ranks whose lengths have no meaningful numerical scale.
chart-table.access: Keep real headers for each column and let the written value carry the measurement. The comparison marks are decorative.
chart-table.content: Name the measured quantity in the numeric header. Use one unit and precision across rows and keep office names in full.
keys: Read the values by row or column using the table navigation of your reading software.

checkbox.use: Let someone choose any number of independent options before submitting a form.
checkbox.avoid: Use RadioGroup when exactly one answer is permitted. Use Switch for a setting that applies immediately.
checkbox.access: Make the text part of the label and expose a mixed state when a parent represents partially selected children.
checkbox.content: Phrase each label as an affirmative choice. Keep the key noun near the beginning and move qualifications into a hint.
keys: Continue to the next or previous control.

code-block.use: Present a complete command, configuration fragment or code example that readers may copy intact.
code-block.avoid: Use inline code for a single prop name within a sentence and Prose for an explanation spanning paragraphs.
code-block.access: Name the snippet with its file name or purpose. Allow keyboard access to horizontal scrolling and give the copy action an accessible name.
code-block.content: Use a concise caption and preserve code exactly in every translation. Put translated explanations outside the snippet.
keys: Activate Copy when the button has focus.
Copy the selected code when clipboard access requires manual copying.

collapsible.use: Hide a short, optional explanation such as how a reference number is assigned.
collapsible.avoid: Keep information needed to complete the current field visible next to that field.
collapsible.access: Use a descriptive summary that toggles with the keyboard. Place controls inside the expanded content rather than inside the summary.
collapsible.content: Write a short question or a specific subject for the trigger. Its meaning should survive when the panel is closed.

combobox.use: Search a long set of permitted values, especially when people know only part of a name.
combobox.avoid: Offer a native select for a few familiar options. Free text without a constrained set belongs in an Input.
combobox.access: Name the input and expose its expanded state and active option. Make it clear when typed text has become a committed choice.
combobox.content: Name the requested entity. Use a short instruction for searching and a specific empty result that points to a next step.

example.good: Search municipality / No matches for Luga

keys: Open the list and move the active option.
Close the list. Tab also moves focus out of the field.

command.use: Search available commands when an experienced user wants to go straight to a known task.
command.avoid: Keep common tasks visible in the ordinary interface so discovery never depends on remembering a shortcut.
command.access: Label the search field and announce the results. Escape should return focus to the invoking control.
command.content: Start each result with the action and name its object. Keep synonyms in search metadata so labels stay short.
keys: Open the command dialog from its trigger.
Filter commands in the search field.
Close the dialog and restore focus.

context-menu.use: Offer shortcuts to actions on a particular document, row or selection.
context-menu.avoid: Keep a visible route to every essential command for people who never use a context click.
context-menu.access: Provide a keyboard invocation and an ordinary actions button. Return focus to the item when the menu closes.
context-menu.content: Name the commands with concise verbs. Include the object when the same action could affect a larger selection.
keys: Open the context menu from its focusable target.
Move to the first or last item.
Focus an item by its label.
Close and restore focus to the invocation target.

currency-chf.use: Set Swiss franc amounts in a ledger, credit note or payment total so that amounts can be compared down a column.
currency-chf.avoid: Use an editable amount field when the reader needs to enter a sum. Cash rounding belongs only on applicable cash totals.
currency-chf.access: Supply the display locale so the spoken minus is in the reader’s language. Keep the amount and its currency together at narrow widths.
currency-chf.content: Name the amount in a short heading and let CurrencyCHF supply the currency and digits. Explain a credit in the adjacent description.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

data-table.use: Let readers reorder comparable records, such as invoices by due date or amount.
data-table.avoid: A fixed tariff schedule with a prescribed reading order only needs Table.
data-table.access: Use the sort button inside the header, expose its direction and translate the sort hint. Compare dates and amounts by their underlying values.
data-table.content: Use the field name as the header, with the unit when needed. Put the sorting instruction in the hint instead of repeating it in every heading.

example.poor: Click here to sort this column

keys: Move to sortable column headings and other controls.
Sort by the focused column. Activate again to reverse the order.
Scroll wide content while its scroll region has focus.

date-picker.use: Choose one nearby date in a form where opening a calendar helps people see weekdays and availability.
date-picker.avoid: Use SwissDate to display an existing deadline in a read-only summary.
date-picker.access: Label the trigger with the purpose of the date. Verify focus returns after a keyboard selection or Escape and the chosen date remains discernible.
date-picker.content: Use a brief noun phrase naming the date’s role. Keep any booking restriction in a separate hint.
keys: Open the picker. Activate a focused day to select it.
Move one day in the calendar grid.
Move to the start or end of the week.
Move one month. Add Shift to move a year.
Dismiss the calendar and return focus to its trigger.

description-list.use: Pair distinct terms with their values in an address, receipt or read-only profile.
description-list.avoid: Repeated records sharing columns belong in a table. Use Prose for a long explanation.
description-list.access: Keep each term adjacent to its description in the DOM and test that their relationship survives the narrow layout.
description-list.content: Use brief, distinct terms. Let long official names wrap in the value column without shortening the source data.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

dialog.use: Interrupt the current view for a focused edit that can be completed or cancelled without navigating away.
dialog.avoid: An optional note belongs in a disclosure. A broad multi-step process benefits from a dedicated page.
dialog.access: Give the dialog a title and a named close control. On dismiss, return focus to a meaningful place in the invoking view.
dialog.content: Name the specific task in the title. Use a short action on each button and a sentence for any explanation.
keys: Open from the trigger or activate a focused action.
Traverse focusable controls inside the open modal.
Close the modal and return focus to its opener.

direction.use: Establish the reading direction of an embedded passage whose script differs from the surrounding interface.
direction.avoid: A change from German to French changes the language but keeps the same reading direction. Set the language tag for that change.
direction.access: Use the correct language and direction on the passage itself. Isolate embedded references or names that use a different script.
direction.content: Preserve names as supplied and use a short caption to identify the translated passage. Keep punctuation inside its language run.

example.good: Original message / [passage in its own direction]
example.poor: Manually reversed characters in the translation

keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

drawer.use: Present a focused task from the edge of the screen, especially on a small device.
drawer.avoid: Put long reading material or multi-stage navigation on a page with a stable URL.
drawer.access: Give the drawer a title and an explicit close button. Opening, completing and dismissing it must work without a drag gesture.
drawer.content: Use a direct title and keep the primary action visible after the instructions wrap. Put one task in each drawer.
keys: Open from the trigger or activate a focused action.
Traverse focusable controls inside the open modal.
Close the modal and return focus to its opener.

dropdown-menu.use: Collect secondary commands that act on the same selected record.
dropdown-menu.avoid: Use a Select to choose a stored value. Keep a frequent primary action visible outside the menu.
dropdown-menu.access: Give the trigger a purpose, support arrow-key movement and restore focus on dismiss. Identify destructive commands with words.
dropdown-menu.content: Use parallel verb phrases, typically one action and one object. Give repeated menus names that include the target record.
keys: Open the menu at its first or last item, then move between items.
Focus the first or last item.
Find an item by the beginning of its label.
Dismiss and return focus to the menu button.
Dismiss and continue in document order.

empty.use: Explain an empty collection and offer the next useful action, such as creating its first address.
empty.avoid: A pending request needs a loading state. A failed request needs an error and a way to retry.
empty.access: Keep the heading and recovery action in reading order. After applying a filter, announce the result count near the search control.
empty.content: Use a short factual heading followed by one next step. Distinguish an empty collection from a search with no matches.

example.good: No invoices yet. Create your first invoice.

keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

field.use: Keep the label, format hint and error for one editor together across validation states.
field.avoid: Several radios or checkboxes sharing a question need a fieldset and legend.
field.access: Pass the supplied control attributes to the real input so its label, description and validation message are linked.
field.content: Name one value, give one concrete format example and use a corrective sentence for an error. Keep the hint separate from the label.

example.good: Reference / Enter the reference shown on your letter.

keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

figure.use: Keep a photograph, diagram or map together with its caption and source.
figure.avoid: An uncaptioned decorative background does not need a figure landmark and credit line in the reading flow.
figure.access: Describe the visual information in the image alternative. Use the caption for context or provenance instead of repeating the alternative.
figure.content: Use one concise caption naming what the reader is seeing. Keep creator and source in a separate credit in each language.

example.good: Station entrance on Bahnhofplatz, seen from the tram stop.

keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

grid.use: Give related blocks a shared edge, such as the name and contact details on an address card.
grid.avoid: A single sequence of fields is easier to maintain in a Stack. Columns can make their reading order ambiguous.
grid.access: Keep the DOM in reading order. Check that the title still precedes the details when the grid collapses to one column.
grid.content: Use a short noun phrase at the head of each field. Allow adjacent columns to grow when the French phrase takes another line.

example.good: Billing address / Route du Lac 8 / 1007 Lausanne
example.poor: Column 2 / Route du Lac 8 / More information

keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

grid-overlay.use: Inspect the placement of columns and baselines while reviewing a layout at real viewport widths.
grid-overlay.avoid: Leave the overlay hidden during ordinary reading and data entry. It is a proofing aid for the interface author.
grid-overlay.access: Preserve keyboard access to the underlying page and provide a way to dismiss the overlay without a pointer.
grid-overlay.content: Name the toggled aid precisely in a short action phrase. Keep the keyboard shortcut separate from the translated label.

example.good: Show layout grid / Ctrl + Shift + G

keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

hover-card.use: Offer an optional preview of a person or record next to a link to its full details.
hover-card.avoid: Keep essential decisions and touch-only actions available by activation elsewhere.
hover-card.access: Make the preview reachable from its trigger by keyboard. Give people a direct way to open the full record outside the preview.
hover-card.content: Use the record name as the title and one identifying detail beneath it. A short destination label can lead to the full record.
keys: Focus the trigger to show the card. Continue to links or controls it contains.
Pin or unpin the card from its trigger.
Dismiss the card. If focus was inside, it returns to the trigger.

iban-input.use: Collect a Swiss account identifier on a payout form where grouping and a checksum help catch transcription errors.
iban-input.avoid: Use a country-aware account field for payments that accept international IBANs beyond the component’s supported scope.
iban-input.access: Keep the account label visible while typing. Give anyone correcting a failed checksum a concrete next step and allow pasting the entire value.
iban-input.content: Use IBAN in every language. Explain the expected country prefix or whose account is required in a separate short hint.

example.good: Account IBAN · Copy it from your bank statement.

keys: Enter or leave the field. A valid identifier is formatted when focus leaves.
Type, select, paste and correct the value with the platform’s editing keys.

icon.use: Identify a familiar action or destination when its compact shape helps people scan a toolbar.
icon.avoid: An unfamiliar symbol for a payment or irreversible action needs a visible text label.
icon.access: Hide a decorative icon from assistive technology. When it is the only visible content of a control, name the control by its action.
icon.content: Write the action or destination in a few words. Avoid describing the geometry of a symbol when naming a control.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

input.use: Collect one short value such as a family name that the person can type or paste.
input.avoid: Use Textarea for correspondence and Select for a closed list of permitted values.
input.access: Associate a persistent label with the input. Preserve the entered value when reporting a validation error.
input.content: Name the value with a noun. Put examples or format instructions on a separate line so the label remains short.
keys: Type, select, paste or replace text with the platform’s editing keys.
Move to the following or preceding control.

input-group.use: Keep a prefix, unit or adjacent action visually attached to one editable value.
input-group.avoid: Several independent questions each need their own label and field instead of a shared border.
input-group.access: Give the editor an explicit label that includes the unit when it matters. Name any adjacent icon button separately.
input-group.content: Keep a fixed prefix short. Put explanations in the label or hint so that units and long translations leave room to type.
keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

input-otp.use: Collect a short verification code delivered through a separate channel when every position belongs to the same value.
input-otp.avoid: Use a password field for reusable credentials of arbitrary length.
input-otp.access: Label the whole code, allow pasting and test one-time-code autofill. Explain how to request a new code when the first expires.
input-otp.content: State the number of digits once in the instruction. Keep delivery and expiry details in a separate sentence.

example.good: Enter the six-digit code from your email.
example.poor: Fill in each box one character at a time.

copy.fr-CH: Saisir le code à six chiffres
copy.it-CH: Inserire il codice a sei cifre
copy.rm-CH: Endatar il code da sis cifras

keys: Enter the code in one input. The visual boxes follow the same value.
Remove digits using native text editing.
Paste the code into the field.

invoice-document.use: Issue a printable, itemised Swiss invoice with its VAT breakdown, total and QR payment section on the same document.
invoice-document.avoid: Use SwissQrBill alone when the surrounding system already produces the complete invoice body.
invoice-document.access: On narrow screens each item shows its description, quantity × unit price, net CHF and VAT without horizontal scrolling. Column and row headings remain available to screen readers. In print, longer invoices repeat their headings.
invoice-document.content: Use a short noun phrase for each service and state its period or quantity when that identifies the charge. Keep the invoice number consistent across the document.
keys: Open the browser print dialog. The document uses its A4 print layout.

item.use: Show the identity and short description of a record in a list, optionally with an action alongside it.
item.avoid: Use a table when values must line up across several comparable columns.
item.access: Give a linked title its own accessible name. Distinguish repeated row actions with the record name.
item.content: Use the identifying name as the title and reserve the second line for one distinguishing fact. Avoid repeating the title in the description.
keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

kbd.use: Show the actual keyboard shortcut for an action already available on screen.
kbd.avoid: A keycap used as the only way to start a task leaves touch and switch users without an action.
kbd.access: Keep a normal focusable control alongside the shortcut and adapt modifier names to the user's platform.
kbd.content: Keep key names short and literal. Translate the description of the action separately from the key sequence.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

label.use: Associate a short, visible name with a specific native control when composing a custom form row.
label.avoid: Use Field when the editor also has hints or errors that need programmatic associations.
label.access: Match htmlFor to the control's unique id. Clicking the label should focus or toggle the intended control.
label.content: Name the requested value in a compact noun phrase. Include a unit when two otherwise identical labels could be confused.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

letter.use: Compose a printable A4 letter with sender, recipient, date, subject and body aligned to an envelope window.
letter.avoid: Use a responsive article for web-only correspondence and InvoiceDocument for itemised charges.
letter.access: Keep the reading order logical independently of the position of the address window. Leave fold marks out of the accessible text and test print at actual size.
letter.content: Use a one-line factual subject and short paragraphs. Keep the recipient’s postal spelling unchanged when translating the body.
keys: Open the browser print dialog. The document uses its A4 print layout.

line-chart.use: Show observations in a meaningful sequence, such as passenger counts across weekdays.
line-chart.avoid: Unordered categories create an invented trend when connected by a line. Compare them with bars instead.
line-chart.access: Describe the time span and unit. Preserve missing observations as such in the supplied data and explain any gaps in the description.
line-chart.content: Use the measured quantity as the title. Keep time labels short and repeat dates consistently throughout a language edition.
keys: Focus the data-table disclosure when readings are available.
Show or hide the same values in the accessible table.

locale-select.use: Let a person switch the language of an application or a specific form using language names in their own spelling.
locale-select.avoid: Use MultilingualField for editing different translations of one piece of content.
locale-select.access: Label the scope of the switch. After a page-wide change, update the document language and retain focus or restore it to an equivalent control.
locale-select.content: Use the language’s own name as its option. Keep the label to a noun phrase that says what will change.
keys: Focus or leave a closed select.
Move through enabled options in the open picker.
Move to the first or last enabled option in the open picker.
Find an option by its label in the open picker.
Confirm the highlighted option and return focus to the select.
Close the picker and keep the previously selected value.

marker.use: Place a state symbol beside a concise name in a schedule or task list.
marker.avoid: A decorative symbol or an unexplained prioritisation code adds noise to a plain list.
marker.access: Provide the written state beside its shape so it remains understandable without colour or vision.
marker.content: Choose one short word or phrase for each state. Keep the same state wording in the legend and the row.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

menubar.use: Organise repeated application commands into familiar groups in a workspace or editor.
menubar.avoid: Use NavigationMenu for ordinary site links where readers expect standard Tab navigation.
menubar.access: Name the menubar and test arrow keys, Escape and focus return across menus. Keep commands available with a keyboard.
menubar.content: Use short category nouns for top-level menus and verbs for commands beneath them. Preserve familiar ordering across translations.
keys: Focus the neighbouring menu or switch groups while a menu is open.
Open a group at the first or last item, then move through its actions.
Focus the first or last item in the current menu.
Open the focused menu or run the focused action.
Dismiss the menu and return to its trigger.

message.use: Identify one contribution to a conversation with a speaker and optional time.
message.avoid: Use a page-level Alert for a system failure outside the exchange.
message.access: Expose the speaker's name for every change of speaker and give timestamps a machine-readable date where available.
message.content: Use the actual sender name followed by a concise statement. Translate role names and keep quoted messages in their original language.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

message-scroller.use: Keep the newest messages visible in a conversation while allowing someone to read older replies.
message-scroller.avoid: Use a paginated or filterable list for an archive people consult by date.
message-scroller.access: Name the log. Test that incoming messages leave the reading position alone when someone scrolls up. Give the jump action an explicit label.
message-scroller.content: Use a short destination for the jump control. Keep sender names and message text separate.
keys: Focus the message log or its jump-to-latest button when available.
Scroll through a log that overflows.
Jump to the latest entry from the button.

multilingual-field.use: Edit several translations of the same title or description and see which languages still need text.
multilingual-field.avoid: Use LocaleSelect when only the language of the interface changes.
multilingual-field.access: Keep each field associated with its language and label. Test moving between languages by keyboard and announcing completion independently of colour.
multilingual-field.content: Write one source phrase per field. Agree a length budget in each language and review the copied wording before publishing.
keys: Switch the active language while a language tab has focus.
Focus the first or last language tab.
Move between the editor and its available actions.
Copy the source text using the button in an empty translation.

native-select.use: Offer one familiar value from a short list on a phone using the device’s own selection interface.
native-select.avoid: Use a searchable combobox when people know the name of a place in a long directory.
native-select.access: Provide a visible Label with htmlFor. Choose a default only when it is a real, reversible choice.
native-select.content: Name the category in one to three words. Write options as nouns in the same grammatical form.

example.poor: Please make your selection from the list below

keys: Focus or leave a closed select.
Move through enabled options in the open picker.
Move to the first or last enabled option in the open picker.
Find an option by its label in the open picker.
Confirm the highlighted option and return focus to the select.
Close the picker and keep the previously selected value.

navigation-menu.use: Move among the top-level sections of a site using links people can bookmark and open in another tab.
navigation-menu.avoid: Use DropdownMenu for commands that change the current item, such as duplicating an invoice.
navigation-menu.access: Give each navigation landmark a distinct name when several are present. Expose the active link with aria-current and retain native link behaviour.
navigation-menu.content: Prefer short destination names. Keep the visible label close to the destination page heading in each language.
keys: Move between visible navigation links and the optional disclosure.
Open or close a collapsed menu from its summary.
Close a collapsed menu that is open and focus its summary.

pagination.use: Navigate between stable pages of records while retaining a shareable position in a list.
pagination.avoid: Use Steps for a sequence of tasks. A short list that fits on one page seldom needs pagination.
pagination.access: Mark the current page and give page-number links meaningful names. Keep the target available to keyboards and touch.
pagination.content: Translate page names and directional actions. A short phrase containing the actual page number works out of context.
keys: Move between links in document order.

phone-input.use: Ask for a Swiss callback number and display it in international +41 format.
phone-input.avoid: Use an international telephone field when contacts may need a foreign number or an extension.
phone-input.access: Use a visible phone label and a telephone keyboard. Make the format hint available after typing and offer a clear correction for the country prefix.
phone-input.content: Say whether the number is for a callback. Keep +41 in the format hint, outside the field name.
keys: Enter or leave the field. A valid identifier is formatted when focus leaves.
Type, select, paste and correct the value with the platform’s editing keys.

popover.use: Reveal optional contextual information or a small control near the element that opened it.
popover.avoid: A consequential choice that blocks the current task belongs in a modal dialog.
popover.access: Give the trigger and panel meaningful names. Check Escape, outside clicks and focus when the panel contains controls.
popover.content: Name the thing being explained. Keep the explanation to a short paragraph and move longer guidance to a linked page.
keys: Open the panel from its trigger or activate a focused action.
Move through the panel and surrounding page.
Close the panel and restore trigger focus.

progress.use: Show how much of an operation has finished when the total can be measured, such as imported records.
progress.avoid: A spinner with an activity label fits work whose completion cannot be estimated.
progress.access: Name the operation. Update its numeric value with measured progress and avoid announcing every percentage point.
progress.content: Use the activity name and a short count or percentage. Pair a completed quantity with its total in all four translations.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

prose.use: Set a guide, policy or long-form explanation with a readable measure, paragraphs, headings and lists.
prose.avoid: Use Grid and Table for dense data or a form that needs field alignment.
prose.access: Use a logical heading hierarchy, meaningful link text and captions for embedded illustrations. Let text resize and reflow on narrow screens.
prose.content: Give each section a descriptive heading and each paragraph one subject. Split long translated sentences at a natural thought boundary.

example.poor: General information and various other things

keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

questionnaire.use: Guide someone through a sequence of short questions with one answer due at each step.
questionnaire.avoid: Show a single form when people need to compare and revise several answers together.
questionnaire.access: Give the questionnaire a distinct name. On step changes, verify focus reaches the new question and earlier answers survive Back.
questionnaire.content: Ask one direct question per step. Use complete choices that still make sense when read without their neighbours.

example.good: How should we contact you? Email / Phone

keys: Move through the answer options and select a radio.
Activate Next, Back, Submit or Edit answers. Focus follows the current question.

radio-group.use: Show a small set of mutually exclusive choices together, for example two ways of receiving an invoice.
radio-group.avoid: Multiple simultaneous choices require checkboxes. A long list with similar names is easier to search.
radio-group.access: Label the group through its legend. The option text must distinguish each choice when read after the same group label.
radio-group.content: Use a short question or noun for the legend. Give options matching forms, such as two delivery methods.
keys: Enter or leave the native radio group.

resizable.use: Let a reviewer widen a document beside its annotations while keeping both panes visible.
resizable.avoid: On a narrow screen, give each pane its own view if neither remains readable at minimum width.
resizable.access: Give the separator a name that identifies the pane being resized. Verify keyboard resizing at both limits and keep the handle visible at high zoom.
resizable.content: Use a short noun phrase for the separator. Translate the pane name consistently with its heading.
keys: Move the divider along its resize axis. Add Shift for a larger step.
Move to the minimum or maximum size.
Collapse or restore the first panel.

scroll-area.use: Constrain a genuinely long panel while keeping the rest of a workspace within reach.
scroll-area.avoid: A short paragraph or a standard form generally reads better with normal page scrolling.
scroll-area.access: Name the region, allow keyboard scrolling and leave room for focus outlines at its edges. Check that scrolling can continue onto the page.
scroll-area.content: Give the panel a short subject label. Distinguish it from nearby scrollable regions using the content it contains.
keys: Scroll a vertical region by a page.

select.use: Offer a short set of known values, such as a preferred delivery method, inside a form.
select.avoid: Use search for a long unfamiliar list where readers need to match part of a name.
select.access: Label the select and preserve the native keyboard interaction. Give the empty option a distinct meaning when the field is optional.
select.content: Use parallel names for the options. Choose one short noun phrase per option and test the longest in its collapsed state.
keys: Focus or leave a closed select.
Move through enabled options in the open picker.
Move to the first or last enabled option in the open picker.
Find an option by its label in the open picker.
Confirm the highlighted option and return focus to the select.
Close the picker and keep the previously selected value.

separator.use: Mark the boundary between two groups of information within the same task.
separator.avoid: A page section with a new subject needs a heading. A line alone gives the reader no topic to navigate to.
separator.access: Leave ornamental rules hidden from assistive technology. Expose a semantic separator only where a boundary carries meaning.
separator.content: The rule has no label in normal reading. Give the following section a short, descriptive heading in each language.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

sheet.use: Edit related information in a modal side panel while retaining the context of the record behind it.
sheet.avoid: Use a full page for long forms that require supporting documents or complex navigation.
sheet.access: Name the panel and close action. Verify that the last input and the footer actions can be reached with a keyboard at high zoom.
sheet.content: Give the panel a short object-specific title. Break longer instructions into field-level hints in each language.
keys: Open from the trigger or activate a focused action.
Traverse focusable controls inside the open modal.
Close the modal and return focus to its opener.

sidebar.use: Provide persistent section navigation beside a set of related workspaces or reference pages.
sidebar.avoid: Use a short row of navigation links if there are only a few destinations and they already fit in the header.
sidebar.access: Name the navigation region and mark the current destination. Make the mobile opener describe what it reveals and support a return to the page.
sidebar.content: Group related destinations under a short heading. Use the same nouns that readers will see as page titles.
keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

skeleton.use: Reserve space for a known heading, row or card while its data arrives.
skeleton.avoid: If the request fails, show an error with recovery. Continuing the placeholder hides the outcome.
skeleton.access: Keep placeholders silent and outside the tab order. Name the loading region once when people need to know why content is absent.
skeleton.content: Leave the placeholder itself empty. A neighbouring status can name the collection in a short phrase.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

slider.use: Adjust a bounded quantity when exploring nearby values is part of the task.
slider.avoid: Use a numeric input for an exact amount that someone must transcribe from an official record.
slider.access: Associate the label, minimum, maximum and current value. Verify the keyboard step matches the precision the task requires.
slider.content: Name the quantity and unit. Pair the thumb with a concise value so the person can read the setting without estimating its position.
keys: Change the value by one step.

sparkline.use: Add a compact trend beside a current reading in a monitoring summary.
sparkline.avoid: Use a full chart if readers need axes, precise comparisons or an explanation of a sudden change.
sparkline.access: Name the quantity, unit and interval in text. Keep the latest observation and data disclosure available independently of the line.
sparkline.content: Pair a brief measure name with its final value. Give the time window in a caption rather than squeezing it into the graphic.

example.poor: A line with no unit or time

keys: Focus the data-table disclosure when readings are available.
Show or hide the same values in the accessible table.

spinner.use: Show that a brief operation is still active while its result is unavailable.
spinner.avoid: Use Progress when the amount of work is measurable. Use a Skeleton when you can reserve the shape of incoming content.
spinner.access: Provide a status label when the spinner is the only feedback. Leave it decorative when the same message is already announced nearby.
spinner.content: Name the activity in a short phrase. Keep the wording factual and avoid promising how long an unknown wait will take.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

stack.use: Space a sequence of controls or paragraphs consistently as their translations wrap.
stack.avoid: Use Grid when rows in neighbouring cards must align to the same tracks.
stack.access: Keep the source order meaningful. Check that wrapping a button group preserves the expected reading and tab order.
stack.content: Group copy that belongs to the same decision. Use one short heading per group and give qualifications their own line.
keys: Move through any links or controls supplied inside the component, in document order.

steps.use: Show progress through a sequence with a defined order, such as submitting an application.
steps.avoid: Use Tabs for peer subjects readers can visit in any order.
steps.access: Label the sequence and mark the current step in text or programmatically. Keep the visual and reading orders identical.
steps.content: Name the task at each step with a short phrase. Put its number outside the translated label so reordering remains possible.

example.poor: Step A / Step B / Step C

keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

swiss-address-form.use: Collect a recipient and a Swiss delivery address, with a locality suggestion after the postal code is entered.
swiss-address-form.avoid: Provide country-specific fields when someone can enter addresses outside Switzerland.
swiss-address-form.access: Keep the postal hint associated with its field. If multiple localities share a code, let the person choose and verify a keyboard-only correction.
swiss-address-form.content: Use the postal abbreviation familiar in each language. Put the four-digit instruction below the label and leave street names in their original spelling.
keys: Move through address fields, locality suggestions and the save button.
Submit the form, or follow a focused error link to its field.
Choose a locality or canton in its native select.

swiss-date.use: Show a filing deadline or an issue date in the reader’s Swiss locale while retaining its machine-readable value.
swiss-date.avoid: Use DatePicker for choosing a date and a time formatter for an appointment time.
swiss-date.access: Pass an unambiguous date or instant to the time element. For a deadline, include its meaning in nearby text so the date has context.
swiss-date.content: Use a short date-role label. Prefer a written month in correspondence where two numeric date conventions might collide.
keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

swiss-postal-code-input.use: Collect a Swiss four-digit postal code as a text identifier, including when another field will capture the locality.
swiss-postal-code-input.avoid: Use an international postal address field for addresses whose codes can contain letters.
swiss-postal-code-input.access: Associate a visible label and four-digit hint with the input. Keep format errors next to it and leave the value available for correction.
swiss-postal-code-input.content: Use PLZ or NPA where familiar and spell out the instruction in plain language. A sample code is four digits without separators.
keys: Paste the code. A full-field paste can include the CH prefix.

swiss-qr-bill.use: Place the Swiss QR payment part and its receipt together beneath a payable invoice.
swiss-qr-bill.avoid: Use InvoiceDocument when a customer also needs line items, the tax breakdown and the amount due.
swiss-qr-bill.access: Keep the human-readable payee, account, reference and amount available alongside the QR code. Verify the physical print at actual size.
swiss-qr-bill.content: Use the supported payment-part language for prescribed headings. Translate the surrounding payment instructions separately and keep them outside the QR code’s clear area.

example.poor: Scan the square for all payment details

keys: Focus the reading-view summary or the scrollable slip when fit is disabled.
Open or close the reading view from its summary.
Scroll the focused slip when it exceeds the available space.

switch.use: Apply a persistent on/off preference immediately, such as receiving appointment reminders.
switch.avoid: A choice collected with other answers for later submission belongs in a checkbox.
switch.access: Keep a stable accessible name in both states and announce the stored state if an update fails.
switch.content: Name the preference in a few words. The control communicates its current value, so the label can stay the same after activation.
keys: Continue to the next or previous control.

table.use: Present records with the same fields so readers can compare a value across rows.
table.avoid: A single invoice summary with distinct labels and values works better as a DescriptionList.
table.access: Use column and row headers as needed. Give the table a caption and keep each unit clear when navigating cell by cell.
table.content: Use a short noun as each header. Put the shared unit in the header and reserve enough space for complete figures.
keys: Use the reading software’s native table commands for rows, columns and headings.
Move between any controls supplied within cells.

tabs.use: Switch among peer views of the same object while preserving its context, such as a case and its documents.
tabs.avoid: Required steps should remain in a sequence. Hiding validation errors behind unrelated tabs makes a form harder to finish.
tabs.access: Name the tablist, associate tabs with their panels and check arrow-key movement. Choose manual activation for slow panels.
tabs.content: Use compact, parallel nouns. Distinguish the labels without suffixes that disappear when space is tight.
keys: Enter the tab list on its active tab. Continue to the panel.
Move between enabled tabs along the list’s orientation.
Move to the first or last enabled tab.
In manual activation mode, display the focused tab’s panel.

text-link.use: Lead to a related document or a stable URL from a paragraph of running text.
text-link.avoid: Use Button when the operation submits or changes the current record without navigating.
text-link.access: Make the link purpose clear in context and retain its visual indicator on keyboard focus. Describe downloads or new windows where readers need to know.
text-link.content: Use the destination’s actual name in the link. Keep punctuation outside the link unless it belongs to the title.
keys: Move between links in document order.

textarea.use: Collect a delivery instruction or another response whose length and line breaks matter.
textarea.avoid: A postal code or date belongs in a field that communicates its expected format.
textarea.access: Keep the label outside the editable area. Make any length limit available before typing and identify the field if a submission fails.
textarea.content: Use a specific prompt. A single sentence can clarify the kind of detail the recipient needs, in each language.

example.good: Delivery instructions / Where can we leave the parcel?
example.poor: Notes / Please enter all other information below.

keys: Type, select, paste or replace text with the platform’s editing keys.
Move to the following or preceding control.

toast.use: Acknowledge a completed action without moving focus away from ongoing work.
toast.avoid: Keep validation errors, payment instructions and information needed later in the page itself.
toast.access: Use a concise announcement. Give people time and keyboard access to any offered action, and keep persistent outcomes discoverable elsewhere.
toast.content: Write one short sentence in the past tense where natural. Name the saved or changed object and omit congratulatory filler.
keys: Focus the dismiss button when supplied. Focus pauses the timer.
Dismiss while focus is in the notification.

toggle.use: Turn a reversible tool or formatting choice on and off while the tool stays in place.
toggle.avoid: Use a Button for a one-time command such as printing, and a Switch for a stored preference that applies immediately.
toggle.access: Keep the name stable and let the pressed state communicate whether the tool is active.
toggle.content: Use one short tool name in both states. Translate the name of the effect, not the inverse action that follows it.

toggle-group.use: Keep two or three peer display modes within reach while the same data stays on screen.
toggle-group.avoid: Use Tabs when each choice opens a separate panel of content.
toggle-group.access: Name the group and each toggle. Ensure a selected state remains perceptible in monochrome and check keyboard movement through the group.
toggle-group.content: Use parallel one- or two-word labels. Repeat the object only in the group name.

example.poor: Select an option: Default / Mode B

keys: Move focus between choices in a horizontal group.
Move through a vertical group or between rows in a grid.
Move to the first or last enabled choice.
Change the pressed state of the focused choice.

tooltip.use: Explain a familiar, focusable control or an abbreviation with a short supplementary hint.
tooltip.avoid: Move required information, links or form controls into the page or a Popover.
tooltip.access: Show the hint on focus as well as hover, allow Escape to dismiss it and give the trigger its own accessible name.
tooltip.content: Use a brief phrase that adds information beyond the control label. Keep the full translated hint readable at high zoom.

example.good: Export / Downloads the filtered rows as CSV

keys: Focus the trigger to display the description, then move away to dismiss it.
Hide the tooltip while keeping focus on the trigger.

trace.use: Expose the sequence of an import or delivery run and let a support engineer open details of individual events.
trace.avoid: Use a progress bar for a single completion percentage with no event history.
trace.access: Give the trace a label describing the operation. Keep each expandable summary meaningful when its details are collapsed.
trace.content: Use past-tense event names of two to five words. Place technical identifiers in the expanded detail.
keys: Focus the summary of an entry with details.

typography.use: Distinguish the page subject, section headings and running text in a programme or reference page.
typography.avoid: A change in text size alone cannot turn a paragraph into a navigable heading.
typography.access: Choose the heading level for its place in the outline. Select its visual size independently and check wrapping at text zoom.
typography.content: Put the subject in the first words of a title. Keep dates and venue details in the following line in every edition.

example.poor: WELCOME / Here is the list you requested

keys: Read in document order. The component has no keyboard command of its own.

uid-input.use: Collect the Swiss enterprise identification number from a supplier’s registration details.
uid-input.avoid: Use AhvInput for a person’s social insurance number. A UID checksum alone cannot establish an enterprise’s current VAT registration.
uid-input.access: Expand the abbreviation in the label or hint and associate the checksum feedback with the field. Keep the CHE prefix visible in the example.
uid-input.content: Use the national abbreviation familiar to the reader. Present the business identifier separately from any VAT suffix.
keys: Enter or leave the field. A valid identifier is formatted when focus leaves.
Type, select, paste and correct the value with the platform’s editing keys.

qr-bill-scanner.use: Read a payment slip when someone needs to transfer invoice details into a local workflow.
qr-bill-scanner.avoid: For creating a payment slip from known billing details, use SwissQrBill.
qr-bill-scanner.access: Offer the file picker alongside the camera and keep payment confirmation available from the keyboard.
qr-bill-scanner.content: Name the file types and explain that the payment details stay on the device.
keys: Move between the file picker, camera and review actions.
Open the native file picker, start the camera, or activate the focused review action.
Cancel reading or review and return focus to the file picker.

file-input.use: Collect documents or images that belong to a specific application or submission.
file-input.avoid: Use an Attachment link to offer a file that is already available for download.
file-input.access: Connect a visible field label. The picker, clipboard paste and remove controls all work with a keyboard. Selection changes are announced.
file-input.content: Name the supporting material and specify accepted formats or size limits beside the field in its own language.

example.good: Attach your PDF proof of residence.

keys: Focus the picker or a selected file’s remove button.
Open the device picker or remove the focused file.
Paste files from the clipboard while focus is in the field.
